subject: Commercial model: usage anchoring, flex credits & negative overage approach
messages:
From: Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@medsys.com>

Cc: procurement@medsys.com

Subject: RFP — commercial clarifications on commits/overages

Rafael,

Thanks for the commercial summary you provided in the RFP packet. Procurement and finance have a couple of follow-ups so we can finalize the pricing appendix for the RFP:

1) We need a concise description of your proposed commit construct (monthly vs. quarterly commit buckets).
2) Please explain how overages are billed and whether any credits can be returned or carried forward if actual usage drops below committed levels later in the contract (our auditors called this "carryback" behavior).
3) We also want an example invoice showing a month where usage spikes then falls below the commit in the next month — how does the math work?

Could you send a short worked example and confirm whether you support negative overage credits (i.e., invoice credits when subsequent months are under-commit)? Also loop in your billing ops and legal if there are special terms.

Best,

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: RFP — commercial clarifications on commits/overages

Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise playbook plus a worked example; attached is an XLS with the same calculations and configurable knobs (pricing_model_v2.xlsx).

Summary of our proposed commercial construct (short):
- Commit type: monthly committed tokens (customer picks monthly baseline) with an option to smooth to quarter for invoicing if preferred. Commit is measured as "billable tokens" per month.
- Unit prices: committed price is the anchored rate (example: $0.003/token for first 20M committed tokens). Overage price applies to tokens beyond the commit in a month (example: $0.004/token).
- Flex credits: for customers with bursty profiles we offer a flex pool. Up to 10% of committed monthly tokens can be auto-borrowed within the month at an intermediate rate (example: $0.0035/token).
- Negative overage (carryback) model: when a month with overage is followed within the same billing quarter by a month with under-commit usage, Redwood will apply a credit to the subsequent invoice up to the value of the prior overage charges, subject to a quarterly reconciliation ceiling equal to 20% of the quarterly committed sum. This prevents gaming while protecting customers with transient spikes.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-up (aggregated commits vs. usage) with invoices monthly and reconciliations applied at quarter close.

Worked example (numbers simplified):
- Committed baseline: 20,000,000 tokens/month at $0.003/token
- Overage rate: $0.004/token
- Flex band: 10% of commit (2,000,000 tokens) at $0.0035/token

Month 1 (Spike): usage = 27,000,000 tokens
- Committed consumed: 20,000,000 @ $0.003 = $60,000
- Flex consumed: 2,000,000 @ $0.0035 = $7,000
- Overage consumed: 5,000,000 @ $0.004 = $20,000
- Month 1 invoice subtotal = $87,000

Month 2 (Soft month): usage = 18,000,000 tokens
- Committed consumed: 18,000,000 @ $0.003 = $54,000 (2,000,000 of commit unused)
- No flex/overage used

Quarterly reconciliation (Months 1–3): assume Month 3 equals commit (20M) for simplicity. Quarterly committed total = 60,000,000 tokens. Quarterly actual usage = 65,000,000 tokens. Net overage across quarter = 5,000,000 tokens.
- Net payable over quarter = 5,000,000 @ $0.004 = $20,000 (already billed in Month 1 as part of the spike).
- Negative overage carryback rule: because Month 2 was under-commit, we apply credits only up to the prior overage amount and within the 20% quarterly ceiling. In this example the quarter still nets to 5M overage, so no credit is returned.

Alternate scenario (larger drop): if Month 2 usage was 12,000,000 tokens (8M under), quarterly actual usage might fall below committed and Redwood would apply a credit to reduce previously billed overages up to the allowable quarterly reconciliation ceiling. The attached sheet shows the algebraic reconciliation used.

Operational notes and guardrails:
- Credit application is limited to the quarter and cannot exceed 20% of quarter commit (prevents indefinite crediting).
- Credits are applied to invoices as negative line items with a clear description ("Overage credit — reconciliation Q4 2026").
- We do not issue cash refunds for overages unless explicitly contracted; crediting is the standard behavior.
- Auditability: every credit has a reconciliation CSV and token-level meter dump available for audit (we include a signed meter report as an attachment on request).

Billing & accounting treatment:
- Monthly invoicing (line-itemized by commit, flex consumption, overage, and credits).
- Quarterly true-up adjustments reflected as credits/debits on the following month's invoice after quarter close.
- Tax and GST handled per local law; invoices include the taxable breakdown and Redwood's W-9/EU VAT registration as required.

Next steps:
- If MedSys is comfortable with the 20% quarterly ceiling and the flex band parameters, we can bake this into the pricing appendix.
- Marissa from Commercial will prepare a redlineable pricing appendix; Karthik is on Cc for any contractual language that needs explicit audit/credit language.

Attached: pricing_model_v2.xlsx, SOW_medsys_draft_v1.pdf

Regards,

Thanks Rafael — the worked example is helpful. Quick follow-ups:

1) For our auditors, can you confirm whether Redwood can provide token-level meter exports that include request id, timestamp, model id, and billed token counts? We need that for internal attribution.
2) For accounting, will credits reduce ARR recognition or be treated as contra-revenue? Your accounting team guidance will determine how we classify.

Can Marissa and Karthik weigh in and share the standard Redwood approach?

Best,
Elena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP — commercial clarifications on commits/overages

Elena — quick answers from Commercial/Finance perspective: 

1) Meter exports: yes. We provide a token-level meter CSV (sftp/secure link) containing request_id, timestamp (UTC), model_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, billed_tokens. We sign these reports and retain them for the contracted retention window (default 12 months, extendable).
2) Accounting treatment: standard practice at Redwood is to treat credits applied in reconciliation as contra-revenue (reduces recognized revenue in the period the credit is applied). We can provide an accounting note for your team showing sample journal entries. If MedSys requires cash refunds instead of credits, we'll need to capture that in the commercial terms and there may be operational lead time.

Operationally, Rafael will update the pricing appendix to call out: quarterly ceiling (20%), flex band (10%), invoice mechanics, and the meter export SLA. We'll also include a sample invoice line layout in the appendix.

Karthik — for legal: please confirm if there are any recommended contractual disclaimers to limit retroactive credits beyond the quarterly ceiling and to preserve audit rights.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
